transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's this cough I can't seem to shake off. It started about three weeks ago, after I'd had a cold, and it just won't go away.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
No, I don't have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
How much is your cough affecting your everyday life?
It's disturbing my sleep most nights, and I'd rate it about a 6 out of 10. I've also noticed I get a bit more breathless than usual when I walk to the shop.
Can you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently, and the dose if you know it?

I take a blue salbutamol inhaler, though I've been using it 4 to 5 times a day lately instead of my usual twice. I also use a Fostair 100/6 inhaler, two puffs twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg once daily for my blood pressure, which I've been on for several years.
Where do you feel the cough most, and does it move or spread to other places?
I can't say I feel it in any particular spot — it's just in my chest, really. I haven't noticed it moving or spreading anywhere else.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make your cough better or worse?
Cold air and talking for a long time seem to set it off. Steam inhalation helps a little.
Besides your high blood pressure, is there anything else in your past health that you think I should know about?
Yes, I've had COPD for about 8 years now. I also smoked 20 cigarettes a day for 40 years, though I stopped 10 years ago.
Besides the breathlessness you mentioned when walking to the shop, is there anything else you've noticed along with your cough?
No, nothing else really. I've not coughed up any blood, I've not lost weight, no night sweats and no chest pain.
What worries you most about this cough?
I'm worried my lungs are getting worse, or that it could be cancer.
Can you tell me what your cough feels like?
It's a wet cough — I'm bringing up white-to-yellow phlegm, more than my usual morning phlegm. The fits tend to last a few minutes at a time.
Is there anything else about your past health — like other illnesses, operations, or hospital stays — that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else. The COPD and my smoking history are the main things.
Is there anything else you take for your health that we haven't talked about yet — including anything you buy without a prescription, like vitamins, supplements, or remedies?
No, nothing like that. Just the inhalers and the lisinopril — I don't take any vitamins or supplements.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
